facts.statement: Tarascosaurus was a relatively small theropod dinosaur measuring between 2.5 and 3 meters in length.
facts.quote: It was a relatively small theropod measuring 2.5 - 3 m long.

facts.statement: The species Tarascosaurus salluvicus was named and described by Buffetaut and Le Loeuff in 1991.
facts.quote: Buffetaut and Jean Le Loeuff named and described these in 1991 as the type species Tarascosaurus salluvicus.

facts.statement: The genus name Tarascosaurus is derived from the Tarasque, a devouring monster from Occitan and Spanish folklore.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from the Tarasque or Tarasca, a devouring monster from Occitan and Spanish folklore.

facts.statement: The specific name salluvicus refers to the Salluvii, a Gallic tribe that inhabited the area near Marseille in antiquity.
facts.quote: The specific name refers to the Salluvii, a Gallic tribe in Antiquity inhabiting the area near Marseille.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen PSL 330201 was found in the Fuvelian Beds dating from the lower Campanian stage.
facts.quote: The holotype PSL 330201 was found in the Fuvelian Beds, dating from the lower Campanian.

facts.statement: A paratype specimen, PSL 330202, consists of two dorsal vertebrae.
facts.quote: PSL 330202, consisting of two dorsal vertebrae, was made a paratype

facts.statement: A damaged tail vertebra, specimen PSL 330203, has been referred to the genus.
facts.quote: Referred was PSL 330203, a damaged tail vertebra.

facts.statement: Tarascosaurus was originally classified within the family Abelisauridae in 1991.
facts.quote: Tarascosaurus was placed in the Abelisauridae in 1991.

facts.statement: In 2003, researchers Allain and Pereda-Suberbiola concluded that the type specimen lacked uniquely abelisaurid traits and should be considered a nomen dubium.
facts.quote: However, in 2003, Ronan Allain and Xabier Pereda-Suberbiola concluded that the type lacked any uniquely abelisaurid traits and that it should be considered a nomen dubium.

facts.statement: In 2003, Oliver Rauhut concluded that Tarascosaurus was a nomen dubium because the available material was not diagnostic.
facts.quote: In 2003, Oliver Rauhut concluded that Tarascosaurus itself was also a nomen dubium because the material was not diagnostic.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analyses conducted in the 2020s support the classification of Tarascosaurus as an abelisaurid.
facts.quote: Phylogenetic analyses in the 2020s also support that it is an abelisaurid.

facts.statement: Tarascosaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 83 to 71 million years ago in the Campanian stage, in what is now Europe.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 83 y 71 millones de años, durante el Campaniense, en lo que hoy es Europa.

facts.statement: Some sources estimate that Tarascosaurus measured approximately 7 to 9 meters in length.
facts.quote: Se calcula que Tarascosaurus medía aproximadamente entre 7 y 9 metros de largo.

facts.statement: Tarascosaurus was the first theropod assigned to the Abelisauridae to be discovered in the Northern Hemisphere.
facts.quote: Fue el primerterópodo asignado a los abelisáurido en ser descubierto en el hemisferio norte.

facts.statement: Tarascosaurus is classified within the Abelisauridae due to its straight femoral neck and cavernous structure of the dorsal vertebrae.
facts.quote: Se lo clasifica dentro de los abelisáuridos debido al cuello del fémur, que es recto, y a la estructura cavernosa de las vértebras dorsales.

facts.statement: The holotype PSL 330201 was found in the Fuvelian Beds, which date to the lower Campanian.
facts.quote: El holotipo PSL 330201 se encontró en los Lechos Fuvelianos, que datan del Campaniense inferior.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of the upper part of a femur that is 22 centimeters long.
facts.quote: Consiste en la parte superior de un fémur, de 22 centímetros de largo.

facts.statement: The femur, with an estimated undamaged length of 35 centimeters, indicates a body length of 2.5 to 3 meters.
facts.quote: El fémur, con una longitud sin daños estimada en 35 centímetros, indica una longitud corporal de 2,5 a 3 metros.

facts.statement: The time range for Tarascosaurus is the Campanian stage, from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)
